summary: Attacked the extraction of Česnavičius, 'Macaulayfication of Noetherian schemes' (Duke Math. J. 170 (2021) 1419–1455; arXiv:1810.04493v2, the last version). The extraction has 81 items, 6 routes and 9 source issues, and REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21 accepted it after heavy corrections. The three recorded source hashes reproduce, and the whole paper was re-read at the TeX. The extraction is sound mathematically. Every numbered statement has an item, and every item statement read against the TeX is faithful. The E9 counterexample, the E5 counterexample and E1–E8 re-derive. Every library citation exists at Mathlib 082e2d3 / Tau Ceti f790474, and Mathlib indeed has no depth, Cohen–Macaulay predicate, excellence, blowup or dualizing complex. Six findings, two medium and four low, none high. (1) The route 1 → route 2 dependency (Kawasaki's Theorem 3.14) and the route 1 → route 6 dependency are not encoded. Since make_queue now builds one design job per Part II parent, the ids used in the briefs will not exist, and DESIGN-SchemeAndStackFoundationsPartII (order 31) can run before DESIGN-DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebraPartII (order 146), the reverse of what the review requires. (2) AS.1, the chosen owner of Noetherian dualizing complexes and local duality, does not plan them. The choice makes the commutative Part II depend on condensed anima. The route's reading of the IKM-24 rejection as confirming AS.1 is wrong. Low: (3) the sheaf-level (S_n) and Cohen–Macaulay predicates (item 16) have no owner. (4) Grothendieck's ascent of formal-fibre properties (EGA IV 7.4.4/7.8.3) has no item, and it overlaps the unreviewed LLL-23/Z79 G-ring item. (5) The blowup dimension bound HIO 12.14 has no item. (6) The 'published version' read is the author's July 2020 manuscript, and the Duke text was never read.

Source, fetched 30 September 2026. The arXiv e-print of 1810.04493v2 has SHA-256 8704c071cf1029ba386764f13841d3871ea79d49c2b2af920086da4789dbd088 (macaulayfication.tex, 2045 lines, and bibliography.ltb). The arXiv PDF v2 has a07d62e6ef1e4c2126c172426391e97031d28006b92ccb6c5f3afd9c2ddb07b9 (24 pp.). The author's file https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~kestutis.cesnavicius/macaulayfication.pdf has 55ded201a17ae161400c1989d67ad7a09356c23f87b2e88eef2e763632939ac6 (24 pp., dated 28 July 2020). All three match the hashes the extraction records. The arXiv abstract page lists only v1 and v2. The author's publications page lists the Duke reference and no corrigendum. The Duke version of record (doi:10.1215/00127094-2020-0063) could not be fetched, because Project Euclid returned a bot block (finding 6).

Whole paper re-read in the TeX (ll. 684–2045): §1 with footnote 1 and §§1.12–1.14; §2 (2.1–2.14 with Remark 2.12's footnote); §3 (Definition 3.1 through Theorem 3.14 with Claims 3.14.5–3.14.6); §4 (4.1–4.4); §5 (5.1–5.5). Page locators were checked in the text layers of both PDFs (pdftotext), including Lemma 2.11 on pp. 7–8, Proposition 3.11 on p. 12, Theorem 3.14 on pp. 14–17, (4.4.1) on p. 19 and Corollary 1.11 on p. 3.

Coverage. Every numbered statement and numbered paragraph (Conjecture 1.1 through Proposition 5.5), and footnote 1, maps to an item among /1–/83. Items /14 and /15 were removed as prose. The inputs the proofs use were checked against the items the review added: Kollár's criterion /67, formal patching /68, ZMT /69, j_* (S_2) /70, EGA I 9.4.7 /71, flat (S_n) /72, local cohomology calculus /76, depth criterion /77, injective hull /78, local duality /79, dualizing-complex facts /80–/81 and Zariski connectedness /82. Two inputs without an item were found: findings 4 and 5. Topics named in the job were checked. Cohen–Macaulay rings, schemes and S_n: /16 and /26 (finding 3). Depth: R03.3. Local cohomology: /38 and /76. Dualizing complexes: /39, /52 and /80 (finding 2). CM-quasi-excellence: /3–/6. Kawasaki's Macaulayfication: /45–/49. Blowups and Rees algebras: /47, /56 and /62. Kawasaki's arithmetic Macaulayfication (Sharp's conjecture): /39. CM locus openness: /26 and /81. Nagata compactification: /13. The main theorems' hypotheses: /7, /57 and /59 (CM-quasi-excellent Noetherian; Proposition 5.2 needs CM-excellent and locally equidimensional; no dualizing complex is assumed globally). Faltings' annihilator theorem is not used in this paper; the annihilator statements are Schenzel's (Remark 3.3, Remark 3.7) and Lemma 3.6.

Item statements. /1–/13, /16–/65 and /66–/83 were compared with the TeX. They are faithful, including the review's rewrites of /12 (E1), /16 (E4), /43 (E5), /45 (E6), /49 (E7) and /55 (E9). The steps of the proofs of Proposition 4.4, Proposition 5.2, Theorem 5.3 and Proposition 5.5 were re-derived. Checked in particular: the GLL hypotheses at each stage of Proposition 4.4; that Z ⊂ X_{R/𝔪^n} with n = N_0·d; the stalk formula through the shift by the coheight δ(x); flatness in Corollary 1.8 through Theorem 5.3(iv); and the dimension-one and dimension ≥ 2 cases of Lemma 2.11.

Source issues. E1 (TeX l. 854 'divisor in $X$') and E2 (l. 873 'ificaiton') were confirmed. E3: the final clause of Lemma 2.11 is never returned to, and the review's extension to Theorem 2.13 holds, since a finite algebra over a complete local ring is a product of complete local rings, which are catenary and hence equidimensional by EGA IV 5.10.9 when (S_2). E4 holds (depth +∞ against dim −∞ off the support). E5's counterexample M = R/(u) ⊕ R over k[[t,u]] with (t,u) was recomputed: it is a d-sequence, the t-torsion is 0 and the tu-torsion is R/(u) ⊕ 0. E6, E7 and E8 were checked at the TeX (ll. 1443, 1550, 1628); in E8 both forms are true, since r_a and r_b act by 0. E9's counterexample A = k[[s,t,u,v,z]]/((s,t)∩(u,v)), K = (z), module (A/K) ⊕ k was recomputed: H⁰_𝔪 = H¹_𝔪 = k, the product of A-annihilators is 𝔪², the preimage is 𝔪² + (z), and z ∉ 𝔪². Both repairs work, because Proposition 4.4 uses only the ideals (j_1,…,j_i). No further mistakes were found; the rest is grammar ('the later', 'the coefficients is').

Library claims. Every declaration cited in the file was looked up in the pinned index and opened at Mathlib 082e2d3 / Tau Ceti f790474, 35 citations in all: IsRegularLocalRing and IsRegularRing (RegularLocalRing/Defs.lean:51, 92); Module.support, Module.annihilator and associatedPrimes; ModuleCat.exists_isRegular_tfae (Depth/Rees.lean:158); ringKrullDim; AlgebraicGeometry.ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_coheight (Properties.lean:376, which is Mathlib's coheight, as the note says); Order.height and Order.coheight; Ideal.height; Submodule.torsionBy and torsionBySet; AdicCompletion; RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular, IsWeaklyRegular and IsWeaklyRegular.of_flat; Scheme.Hom.normalization; Module.supportDim and the three KrullDimension/Regular.lean lemmas (:141, :151, :182, as stated); localCohomology, ofSelfLERadical, isoSelfLERadical and isoOfSameRadical (LocalCohomology.lean:175, 180, 229, 263; the last two need [IsNoetherian R R]; the file's 'Future work' list names the derived-functor, Čech and long-exact-sequence descriptions); reesAlgebra; Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat; Scheme.Hom.exists_isIso_morphismRestrict_toNormalization (ZariskisMainTheorem.lean:206, Grothendieck's form); Scheme.PartialIso and Scheme.Birational (Birational.lean:39, 181; this is equivalence, not a morphism predicate); Scheme.Hom.image (IdealSheaf/Subscheme.lean:661); TauCeti.IsInjectiveEnvelope (Envelope.lean:101, whose docstring says existence is not proved); Submodule.colon (Ideal/Colon.lean:35, ideal-valued).

Absence claims. The declaration index and both source trees were searched for depth, Cohen–Macaulay, catenary, excellent, Nagata, Japanese, dualizing, blowup, formal fibre, equidimensional, Serre condition, d-sequence, system of parameters, Gorenstein, injective hull and Matlis. Mathlib's only depth-related files are RingTheory/Depth/Rees.lean and a deprecated stub RingTheory/Regular/Depth.lean. Mathlib has no Cohen–Macaulay, excellence or blowup declarations, so the 'no depth, no Cohen–Macaulay predicate, no excellence and no blowups' claim holds. Tau Ceti has Krull–Akizuki (RingTheory/IntegralClosure/NormalizationFinite.lean, which says it has no IsNagata, IsJapanese or IsExcellent), injective envelopes without existence, and CodimensionOnePoint. None changes a status.

Planned statuses and cited layers, read in full: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3 and P9, with the integrated R03.3 depth node; SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 and SF.4; AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L2, with its integrated Nagata node and gap, and L5; AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry A0-extension and R09.7a; AdicSpacesPartII F0; AnalyticStacks AS.1 (research/blueprint/roadmaps/AnalyticStacks.json); and the Tau Ceti layers StableReduction 2 and 4, JacobianChallenge C, ModularCurves 4D and StablePeriodicCurved 7. /13 is planned in L2 (the nonnoetherian Nagata statement), /62 in StableReduction Layers 4 and 2 (flat base change), /73 in JacobianChallenge C and /75 in L2 with Mathlib's Hom.image. /16 is only partly planned (finding 3). The external UPSTREAM:ECD:SCH_SUPPORT_NOETH, integration owner SF.2, was checked as L2's Noetherian supplier.

Routes and duplication. Checked against the other extractions and reviews: PAPER-ANDRE-18-B (big CM algebras; DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay; R03.3 local cohomology and Matlis), PAPER-BHATT-18 (SF.4 blowup domination and flattening), PAPER-TEMKIN-17 (normalisation and flattening in L5; resolution of quasi-excellent threefolds in PrimeToDegreeAlterations), PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23 and PAPER-HACON-WITASZEK-23 (AS.1 dualizing, R03.3 cm-depth), PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19 (SGA 2 VIII 2.3 on SF.4), PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 (review of route 3), PAPER-BOCKLE-IYENGAR-PASKUNAS-23 (universally catenary) and PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23 (G-rings; partial, unreviewed). A scan of every extraction's items for quasi-excellence, universal catenarity, formal equidimensionality, Ratliff and Macaulayfication finds no other owner of routes 1–2 material, except the overlaps in findings 2 and 4. The design queue was checked: make_queue.py paper_designs, queue.json, and issues #3361 and #3476 (finding 1).

Prerequisites. All 14 DOIs in the file were resolved through Crossref and match their citations, including the review's corrections: Deligne 10.1215/0023608X-2010-009 is 'Le théorème de plongement de Nagata'; GLL is 'Hypersurfaces in projective schemes and a moving lemma'; Kollár is 'Coherence of local and global hulls'; Heitmann is RMJ 12 (1982); Heinrich is JCA 9 (2017).

findings.claim: Route 1 depends on route 2 (it imports Theorem 3.14, Proposition 3.11 and the module blowups, items 45–49) and on route 6 (the avoidance lemma, item 53). Neither dependency is encoded, and the queue cannot honour either as the file states it. (a) Route 1's `prerequisites` list does not name its sibling Part II or the arithmetic-presentation Part II, although its brief says it 'starts after … KawasakiCohenMacaulayBlowingUps' and imports from 'SchemeAndStackFoundationsPartIIArithmeticPresentation'. (b) Since 28 September 2026, make_queue.py builds one design job per Part II parent. Route 1 and route 6 therefore become one job, DESIGN-SchemeAndStackFoundationsPartII, together with seven other continuations. Route 2 becomes DESIGN-DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebraPartII. No roadmap with the ids MacaulayficationOfNoetherianSchemes, KawasakiCohenMacaulayBlowingUps or SchemeAndStackFoundationsPartIIArithmeticPresentation will exist, so the brief's imports by id point to nothing. (c) Both design jobs are open at once with no ordering: the Scheme Part II job is order 31 and the commutative Part II job is order 146, and neither has 'after'. The review's own requirement ('Route 2 must be designed before route 1') can therefore be violated. The consumer is more likely to be designed first. (d) The review's reason for copying PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23's brief into route 6 ('make_queue.py keeps one brief per shared design id, and the later paper in papers.json wins') no longer describes the queue.

findings.claim: The owner chosen for the Noetherian dualizing complexes and local duality does not plan them, and the choice gives a heavy dependency to pure local algebra. AS.1's contract covers Scholze's Lectures VII–VIII: locally compact spaces, the quasi-coherent six-functor formalism on derived schemes, Grothendieck–Serre duality for proper smooth maps, and D-modules. Its text plans no dualizing complex of a Noetherian ring, no D^b_coh duality, no normalisation and no local duality. Item 39's own note concedes this: 'AS.1's own text does not plan it'. Routing items 39, 79 and 80 there puts the purely commutative route 2 (Lemma 3.6, and through it Proposition 4.4) downstream of AS.0 and of SolidAnalyticRings SA.0 (light condensed anima), EnhancedDerivedSheaves E1/E5:animation and DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.2. The route 5 reason also cites the rejection of PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 route 3 as 'confirm[ing] the choice'. That misreads it: that review rejected the route because the duality package is 'not explicitly in the named stage contracts', and it left 'generic local duality/Tate ownership' unresolved. The same objection applies to AS.1.

Resolve G2, complete G1, and then split or extend the supplier precisely.' Route 1 there: 'generic local duality/Tate ownership and cited-source closure remain unresolved'. The only uses in the paper are for Noetherian local rings and schemes: §3.5 (Stacks 0A7B–0A7I, 0DW7), Lemma 3.6 (local duality, Hartshorne RD V 6.2) and §4.2.

findings.claim: The sheaf-level notions of §1.14 have no owner. These are: the support of a coherent module as the closed subscheme cut out by its annihilator; (S_n) and Cohen–Macaulay coherent O_X-modules; (S_n) and Cohen–Macaulay schemes. The last is the predicate in the conclusion of Theorem 1.6. Item 16 is marked planned, and its note says 'Only the sheaf-level form is an addition, which route 1 states as an adapter'. But R03.3 plans only finite modules over rings, SF.0 only quasi-coherent modules, and route 1's brief does not construct the adapter. It lists 'the Serre conditions' among what it imports from R03.3 and omits the sheaf-level predicates from 'Construct here'.
findings.evidence: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3 (data/atlas.json): 'Develop regular sequences, depth, Cohen–Macaulay rings/modules, projective dimension, Auslander–Buchsbaum … Give equidimensionality, associated-prime and support lemmas for finite modules.' SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0: 'Construct schemes, quasi-coherent modules and relative Spec/Proj …'. The (S_k) precedent cited in item 16's note, PAPER-HACON-WITASZEK-23/cm-depth, is stated 'For finite modules over Noetherian local rings'. In the paper, §1.14 (p. 4; TeX ll. 887–895) reads: 'A scheme X is (S_n) or Cohen–Macaulay if it is locally Noetherian and O_X has the respective property as an O_X-module'. Route 1's brief imports 'R03.3 for depth, Cohen–Macaulay modules, the Serre conditions …', and its 'Construct here' paragraph names no sheaf-level (S_n) or Cohen–Macaulay predicate.
findings.fix: Add to route 1's 'Construct here' paragraph the stalkwise sheaf-level definitions: Supp(𝓜) as the closed subscheme of Ann_{O_X}(𝓜); (S_n) and Cohen–Macaulay coherent modules with the E4 convention (x ∈ Supp(𝓜)); (S_n) and Cohen–Macaulay locally Noetherian schemes. Take them together with item 26's loci U_{(S_n)}(𝓜) and CM(𝓜), and import the module-level notions from R03.3. Change item 16's note to name route 1 as the owner of the sheaf-level part.

findings.claim: Grothendieck's theorem that properties P of formal fibres ascend along morphisms locally of finite type (EGA IV₂ 7.4.4, with 7.3.8 for P = Cohen–Macaulay or (S_n)) has no item and no supplier. It is a substantial theorem hidden in citations. The case P = regular (quasi-excellence ascends, EGA IV₂ 7.8.3) is used in the proof of Proposition 2.7, 'Since X̃ inherits quasi-excellence', but no item states it: item 1 gives only the definitions and the openness of Reg(X). Item 6 (P = CM) and item 28 (P = (S_n)) state the stability as remarks, with the theorem only as a citation. The unreviewed, partial extraction PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23 proposes the regular case (G-rings are stable under essentially finite type maps, item Z79) for SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4. So the same theorem is heading for two owners.
findings.evidence: Paper, p. 2 (TeX l. 789), Remark 1.5: 'If X is CM-quasi-excellent, then so is every localization of a locally finite type X-scheme thanks to [EGA IV₂, 7.4.4 (with 7.3.8)] for (1) and [EGA IV₂, 6.11.9 (i)] for (2).' Proof of Proposition 2.7, p. 6 (TeX l. 1016): 'Since X̃ inherits quasi-excellence, Lemma 2.5 implies its formal equidimensionality, and so excellence.' §2.10, p. 7: '(S_n)-quasi-excellence is stable under localization and ascends along morphisms that are locally of finite type.' PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23.result.json item Z79, 'G-rings and their stability under essentially finite type maps', is missing, with sources Stacks 07GH and 07PV. It sits on a source route to SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0/SF.1/SF.4/SF.5, and that extraction has status partial and no review.json. A search of data/atlas.json stage texts for 'formal fib', 'G-ring' and 'excellen' finds no layer planning the ascent theorem.
findings.fix: Add an item: 'EGA IV₂ 7.4.4: if the formal fibres of the local rings of a locally Noetherian X have property P (P ∈ {regular, Cohen–Macaulay, (S_n)}, with the axioms of 7.3), then so do those of every X-scheme locally of finite type'. Give it the P = regular corollary (quasi-excellence ascends, EGA IV₂ 7.8.3(ii)), and cite it from items 1, 6, 25 and 28. Put it on route 1 and have route 1's brief plan it once for all three P. Note for the maintainer: reconcile with PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23/Z79 when that extraction is reviewed, so that the G-ring case and the CM/(S_n) cases have one owner.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21.result.json: item PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-21/49 (proof of Theorem 3.14) and route 2's brief
findings.claim: The dimension bound for blowing up, dim Bl_I(Supp M) ≤ dim Supp(M) (Herrmann–Ikeda–Orbanz 12.14), is the first step of the proof of Theorem 3.14. It reduces Cohen–Macaulayness to depth ≥ dim Supp(M) at closed points. It appears only in item 49's list of references and is neither an item nor attributed to a supplier. StableReduction Layer 4, which route 2 imports for blowups, plans no dimension statement. The bound needs the dimension theory of Rees algebras (dim R[It] ≤ dim R + 1) and is not routine.
findings.evidence: Paper, proof of Theorem 3.14, p. 14 (TeX l. 1533): 'By the universal property of blowing up (or by [SP, 080E] directly), this schematic image is the blowing up of Supp(M) at the restriction of I. In particular, by [HIO88, 12.14], its dimension is ≤ dim(Supp(M)).' tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction Layer 4 (content/tau-ceti/StableReduction/README.md:470): 'Construct the Rees algebra and the blowup … Prove the universal property, properness/projectivity, compatibility with flat base change, behaviour away from the centre, exceptional divisor, strict transform, and affine chart descriptions.' It has no dimension clause. Mathlib at 082e2d3 has reesAlgebra (RingTheory/ReesAlgebra.lean:39) and reesAlgebra.fg (:107) but no dimension formula for it.
findings.fix: Add an item on route 2: 'For a Noetherian local ring R, a finite R-module M and an ideal I, dim Bl_I(Supp M) ≤ dim Supp M (HIO 12.14; via dim R[It] ≤ dim R + 1)'. Name it in item 49's proof and in route 2's 'Construct here' list, unless the design job finds it planned in R03.3's dimension formulas.

findings.claim: The file called 'the author's copy of the published version' is the author's final manuscript dated 28 July 2020. It predates arXiv v2 (3 September 2020) and is not the Duke typeset text (Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 7, pp. 1419–1455). Neither the extraction nor the review read the version of record. The statements that 'both carry the two misprints' and that the published and arXiv texts are 'the same' therefore compare two author-produced texts. They say nothing about the published text, where copy-editing may have fixed E1 ('divisor in X', in the statement of Corollary 1.11) or E2. The file has no `sourceVersions` record saying so.
findings.evidence: The recorded file (https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~kestutis.cesnavicius/macaulayfication.pdf, SHA-256 55ded201…9ac6, re-fetched on 30 September 2026) prints on p. 1 'Date: July 28, 2020.'. Its PDF metadata give CreationDate 'Tue Jul 28 08:16:22 2020 UTC' and 24 pages; the Duke page range is 37 pages. The arXiv abstract page lists v1 and v2 (v2 is the recorded a07d62e6…07b9 file). https://doi.org/10.1215/00127094-2020-0063 redirects to projecteuclid.org, which returned an Incapsula bot-block page instead of the text on 30 September 2026. The extraction's readSections say 'the author's copy of the published version … whose listing on the author's publications page records Duke Mathematical Journal 170 (2021)'. That page lists the manuscript under the Duke reference but does not make it the version of record. The review has 'the author's publications page, which lists no corrigendum' and 'a word-by-word comparison of the published and arXiv texts, which are the same'.
findings.fix: Describe the file as 'the author's final manuscript (dated 28 July 2020)'. Add sourceVersions: an 'author copy' entry for it and a 'preprint' entry for arXiv v2 with their hashes, and a note that the Duke text was not read because Project Euclid refuses automated access. Scope E1–E9 ('known': new) to those two texts. Add the paper to research/blueprint/collation/REQUESTS.md, so that E1 and E2, which quote the printed statement of Corollary 1.11 and §1.13, are checked against the Duke text.
